original_question: A pro-p group is(relatively) strictly finitely presented if it is the pro-p completion of a group that is finitely presented(respectively, finitely presented in some finitely-based variety of groups). A pro-p group is finitely axiomatizable if it is determined up to isomorphism by a single sentence in the first-order language of group theory. (a) Does there exist a(relatively) strictly finitely presented pro-p group that is not finitely axiomatizable in the class of all pro-p groups? (b) In particular, is every finitely generated free pro-p group finitely axiomatizable? See(A. Nies, K. Tent, D. Segal, Proc. London Math. Soc. (3), 123(2021), 597– 635; D. Segal, Preprint, 2025, https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04816).
target_in_paper: Problem 21.120 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of The Kourovka Notebook.
correct_elements: Your draft matches the paper's official problem almost verbatim. It correctly includes the two definitions used in the paper: '(relatively) strictly finitely presented' for pro-p groups, and 'finitely axiomatizable' as determination up to isomorphism by a single first-order sentence in the language of groups. It also correctly preserves both parts of the problem: the existence question in (a) and the special case about finitely generated free pro-p groups in (b), together with the motivating references cited by the paper.
missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, it helps to make the quantifier over the prime explicit: part (a) asks for existence of such a pro-p group for some prime p, while part (b) asks about every finitely generated free pro-p group, i.e. for every prime p and every finite rank.
In part (b), the ambient class should be made explicit: 'finitely axiomatizable' means finitely axiomatizable within the class of all pro-p groups, not among all groups or all profinite groups.
For complete self-containment, 'finitely generated free pro-p group' can be spelled out as the free pro-p group F_d on d topological generators, with d finite.
refined_question: For some prime p, does there exist a pro-p group G that is (relatively) strictly finitely presented—meaning that G is the pro-p completion of a finitely presented discrete group, respectively of a discrete group finitely presented in some finitely based variety of groups—but is not finitely axiomatizable, i.e. is not determined up to isomorphism within the class of all pro-p groups by a single first-order sentence in the language of groups? In particular, for every prime p and every d >= 1, is the free pro-p group F_d on d topological generators finitely axiomatizable within the class of all pro-p groups?
justification: The draft is essentially a transcription of the notebook's official open problem. The paper itself states the two definitions and then asks exactly the two-part question reproduced in your draft. The only useful sharpening is to make explicit the quantification over the prime p and the finite rank in the free pro-p case, and to restate clearly that the relevant notion of finite axiomatizability is within the class of all pro-p groups.
